tips.q: How do I write a cinematic portrait prompt?
tips.a: Stack five layers: genre ('film noir' / 'cyberpunk'), lighting ('chiaroscuro key light' / 'golden hour rim'), lens ('50mm f/1.4, shallow DOF'), film stock ('Kodak Portra 400, fine grain'), and mood ('moody, contemplative'). Combine all five — that's what separates cinematic from generic portrait.

tips.q: Which lighting keywords work best (golden hour, neon rain, film noir)?
tips.a: Golden hour gives warm rim light + soft skin glow. Neon rain produces saturated magenta/cyan reflections on wet surfaces. Film noir means hard key + deep shadow + black-and-white. Pick the one matching your mood, then add a secondary cue like 'practical lights in background' to add depth.

tips.q: How do I keep my face recognizable across stylized portraits?
tips.a: Add 'preserve facial features, hairstyle, and skin tone exactly' to every prompt and upload a sharp 1024px+ reference. Avoid pushing genre keywords like 'anime' or 'cartoon' that override likeness. Heavy stylization (fantasy, vintage Hollywood) needs a stronger reference photo than realistic styles.

tips.q: What aspect ratio is best for editorial vs phone wallpaper?
tips.a: 4:5 is the editorial sweet spot — magazine covers, LinkedIn featured, Instagram portrait. 9:16 is for phone wallpaper, Reels, and TikTok. 3:4 works for poster prints and dating-app vertical crops. GPT Image 2 supports all three natively at 2K so detail holds up at print size.

faq.q: What makes a cinematic portrait prompt?
faq.a: Five elements: (1) lighting cue ('chiaroscuro' / 'golden hour' / 'neon key light'), (2) camera/lens ('shot on 50mm f/1.4' / 'shallow depth of field'), (3) film/grain ('Kodak Portra 400' / 'film grain'), (4) mood ('moody noir' / 'dreamy haze'), (5) composition ('close-up portrait' / 'editorial framing'). Combine all five for cinematic feel.

faq.q: How do I turn my photo into a movie poster portrait?
faq.a: Upload your photo, paste a cinematic prompt that names the genre ('film noir' / 'sci-fi' / 'fantasy hero'), specify the lens (50mm / 85mm), lighting (key + fill), and mood. GPT Image 2 keeps your face accurate while transforming the atmosphere.

faq.q: What's the best cinematic portrait prompt for ChatGPT / GPT Image 2?
faq.a: Reliable template: 'Cinematic close-up portrait of [me/subject], [genre] aesthetic, [lighting setup], shot on 50mm lens at f/1.4, shallow depth of field, [color palette], film grain, [mood], moody atmosphere.' Adjust genre and color palette for the specific look.

faq.q: Can GPT Image 2 do realistic skin texture in portraits?
faq.a: Yes — its image-to-image mode preserves real skin pores, micro-shadows, and natural blemishes when you upload a reference photo. Add 'realistic skin texture, natural skin tones, no plastic smoothing' to the prompt to lock this in.

faq.q: How is cinematic portrait different from regular portrait prompts?
faq.a: Regular portraits aim for clean / flattering / studio look (LinkedIn-ready). Cinematic portraits aim for narrative / mood / film aesthetic (movie poster, character feel). Different lighting (one-direction key light vs even softbox), different color (graded vs neutral), different intent (storytelling vs identity).
